messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx spike detected from prefix-cache-proxy cluster (us-west-2). 5xx rate > 7% over the last 5m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/d/ops/cache-5xx

devon: I'm paged, looking now :mag:

maria: I can see the spike in router logs. lots of gateway timeouts and 502/500s coming from prefix-kv-01 nodes. Latency tail also increased (~p99 1.2s -> 3.8s).

devon: grabbing logs from prefix-kv-01. snippets show repeated eviction errors and a cascade of misses.

devon: ```
2026-03-15T02:12:23Z prefix-kv-01 ERROR evict: excessive_evictions count=1245 prefix=/customer/ingest/abcd
2026-03-15T02:12:24Z prefix-kv-01 WARN cache_miss_stream spike=72%
2026-03-15T02:12:24Z prefix-kv-01 ERROR runtime: panic: nil pointer dereference
```

maria: that runtime panic explains some 500s. looks like a metadata path hit a nil. not full corruption yet but unstable.

ingrid: customer-facing impact? checking frontend telemetry. Several batch inference routes showing 503/504s. estimated affected traffic ~6% global, concentrated in us-west.

ben: quick mitigation plan: 1) enable origin fallback for prefixes where miss rate > 85% 2) scale kv cluster by +2 replicas 3) throttle the bulk ingest job that is churning prefixes. I'll run the commands.

ben: ```sh
# enable fallback to origin for high-miss prefixes
infractl set-config prefix-cache.fallback_threshold=0.85 --service=prefix-cache
# scale KV cluster
infractl scale kv-prefix-cluster --replicas 4 --region us-west-2
# throttle bulk job (kubernetes cron)
kubectl patch cronjob ingest-weights -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' -n data-pipelines
```

incident-bot: ACTION: Config change applied, starting canary rollout in us-west-2.

devon: canary metrics: 5xx in canary down from 7.3% -> 1.1% in 4m. No new panics observed in canary nodes. Rolling to remaining nodes now.

maria: found a correlation: the bulk ingest job wrote many tiny prefixes with very short TTLs which caused constant insert/evict churn. eviction queue flooded the workers and we saw OOM-like backpressure and panics.

ben: paused the bulk job. warming cache for the most common prefixes from S3 snapshot. rehydration started. 5xx dropping overall to ~0.9% but some retry storms persist.

ingrid: customer impact assessment: enterprise customers XCorp and YFinance saw elevated errors for ~18 minutes. internal SLOs impacted for the batch-inference route. Ops ticket created: OPS-6428. Need comms to affected accounts.

devon: handoff notes (I'll stay until handoff):
- root cause: eviction storm driven by high-write small-prefix pattern from ingest-weights -> KV workers thrashing -> runtime nil pointer panic in prefix-kv handler
- mitigations applied: pause job, enable origin fallback, scale KV replicas, cache warmup from snapshot
- immediate next steps: patch eviction heuristics (increase backoff + sampling), add write-rate alert on prefix namespace, debug the nil pointer stacktrace and add defensive checks

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: @sre-rotation will take over at 2055018690. Please add summary + links to timeline.

sre-rotation: taking over. added myself to OPS-6428. I'll coordinate the postmortem and schedule a follow-up with infra and data-pipeline owners.

ben: note: we detected a small metadata inconsistency when snapshotting — nothing indicates data loss, but we exported metadata and checkpoints to gs://redwood-ops/ops-6428/metadata-dump for deeper analysis.

maria: runbook snippets used during mitigation:```
# fallback
infractl set-config prefix-cache.origin_fallback=true --env production
# pause job
kubectl patch cronjob ingest-weights -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' -n data-pipelines
# scale cluster
infractl scale kv-prefix-cluster --replicas 4 --region us-west-2
```

devon: action items for post-incident: [1] commit eviction backoff PR + canary (owner: devon), [2] add alert on prefix write rate (owner: data-pipelines team), [3] fix nil-pointer defensive checks in prefix-kv handler (owner: eng-runtime), [4] customer comms draft (owner: ingrid).

ingrid: I'll draft customer note and sync with comms. ETA 60m.

devon: closing live mitigation: system stable, 5xx returned to baseline (~0.2%) after full rollout and pause of the job. leaving detailed root-cause and timeline to postmortem. thanks for fast triage everyone :thumbsup:
note: TLDR: eviction storm from bulk ingest caused KV thrash -> runtime panics -> elevated 5xx. mitigations: pause job, enable origin fallback, scale KV, cache warmup. handoff to oncall for postmortem and customer comms.
